flags.title: SNAP ABAWD Work Requirements — Active Statewide
flags.trigger: state=OH AND benefit_type=SNAP AND age>=18 AND age<=54
flags.message: Ohio SNAP ABAWD work requirements are fully active — no statewide waiver. ABAWDs ages 18-54 must document 80 hours/month of work, education, job training, or qualifying volunteer activity. Waiver expired 2023. Surface exemptions immediately: documented disability, caregiving for dependent, pregnancy, enrollment in job training, participation in SNAP E&T program. Rural counties may qualify for county-level exemptions — check Ohio JFS ABAWD county list at jfs.ohio.gov.

flags.title: Ohio Medicaid Expansion — Covered, But Work Requirement Proposed
flags.message: Ohio expanded Medicaid in 2013 — adults 19-64 to 138% FPL qualify with no coverage gap. As of 2025, Ohio has proposed but not implemented Medicaid work requirements (blocked in federal court historically). Monitor jfs.ohio.gov for status changes. Managed care plans: CareSource, Molina, Buckeye Health Plan, UnitedHealthcare Community Plan, Anthem. Always verify managed care plan enrollment before routing specialty care.

flags.title: Ohio Minimum Wage $10.45/hr — Far Below Living Wage
flags.message: Ohio minimum wage is $10.45/hr (2025) — among the lowest in the Midwest. Federal minimum is $7.25/hr (Ohio supersedes). No major Ohio city has enacted a higher local minimum wage (preemption by state law). Wage theft is epidemic in Ohio's food service, care work, and construction sectors. Any worker earning close to minimum wage in Ohio is likely being underpaid relative to cost of living — always calculate hours and check for overtime violations.

flags.title: Ohio TANF (Ohio Works First) — $536/mo Max, 36-Month Lifetime Limit
flags.message: Ohio TANF (Ohio Works First / OWF) pays up to $536/month for a family of 3. CRITICAL: Ohio uses a 36-month lifetime limit — shorter than the 60-month federal limit. If a client has prior TANF history in Ohio, verify remaining months immediately before routing. Work requirement: 30 hours/week (20 for single parent with child under 6). Never present OWF as standalone — always pair with SNAP, Medicaid, CCAP, HEAP, and emergency assistance.

flags.title: Ohio HEAP — Opens November 1
flags.message: Ohio HEAP application opens November 1 each year for heating season. HEAP Crisis Component available year-round for imminent shutoff. Income limit: 175% FPL (higher than many states). Administered by local Community Action Agencies — 50+ agencies statewide. Columbia Gas Ohio and AEP Ohio shutoff protections run October 15-April 15 (winter moratorium). Duke Energy Ohio: contact directly for winter shutoff protection program.

flags.title: Ohio Eviction Process — 3-Day Notice + Expedited Hearing
flags.message: Ohio has one of the fastest eviction timelines in the country. Landlord can serve 3-day notice to vacate (non-payment) with no cure period required. After 3-day notice expires, landlord files in Municipal or County Court. Hearing can be scheduled as soon as 3-7 days after filing. Total timeline: as fast as 10-14 days from notice to writ of restitution. Contact legal aid IMMEDIATELY when any eviction notice is served — do not wait for hearing date. Ohio does not require written leases for month-to-month tenancies.

flags.title: Ohio UI — 21-Day Appeal Deadline (Shorter Than Region)
flags.message: Ohio unemployment insurance maximum duration is 26 weeks but actual duration is determined by base period wages. Ohio UI appeal deadline: 21 days from mailing date of determination — shorter than IL (30 days) and NY (30 days). Contact legal aid within 10 days of any denial. Ohio's UI system (JFS) has chronic backlogs and denial rates — appeal virtually every denial.

flags.title: Ohio OCRC — 2-Year Civil Rights SOL, Broader Than Federal 300 Days
flags.message: Ohio Civil Rights Commission (OCRC) has a 2-year statute of limitations for employment and housing discrimination complaints — significantly longer than EEOC/HUD's 300-day federal deadline. This is a major strategic advantage: Ohio workers and tenants who missed the federal 300-day deadline may still have a valid state claim. Always file with OCRC even after federal deadlines expire. OCRC workshares with EEOC for employment claims.
action_items: File with OCRC even if federal deadline missed
File EEOC simultaneously if within 300 days

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Ohio Emergency Admission
flags.message: OH involuntary psychiatric hold law: Ohio Emergency Admission. Statutory authority: ORC § 5122.10. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in OH retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in OH: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Ohio Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Ohio Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
